decisions.adr: ADR 0041 — Five widths and two spellings
decisions.selected_review: Retain its selected BX/EX implementation as a nesting depth. Section depth produces the source-required nested behavior, and current tests distinguish nesting, inside/outside silence, and resumption after a matched EX. Its historical note that there were no pixel tests remains accurate for the current test file; this shard supplies a scratch-only independent raster assertion draft. No malformed unmatched-pair policy is attributed to the ADR or ISO.
decisions.evidence: §7.8.2 physical p.126 / printed p.111 and Table 33 physical p.127 / printed p.112; ADR 0041; code in run.rs and Machine.compatibility; tests in content_streams.rs.

decisions.selected_review: The existing producer-side classification remains appropriate. EC3 #732 makes URL a required producer entry, but does not turn omission into a required reader refusal. Keeping an extension with no URL while representing `url: None` is an explicit tolerance policy; the current test fixture verifies the extension-array parser still reads that item. #399's BaseVersion comparison is likewise a producer constraint not checked by this parser. #239 demotes time-order monotonicity to should. No writer currently emits extensions, so no claim of producer conformance is grounded.
decisions.evidence: §7.12.1–.6 physical pp.156–158 / printed pp.141–143, primary annotation images for pages157–158; Annex E physical pp.892–893 / printed pp.877–878 with #229/#340; requirements.rs and its unit assertions; prior Annex E feature-ledger review.

decisions.selected_review: Annex E.1 routes unsupported developer-feature handling to Annex I; no reader must reject a file solely because the prefix is unrecognized. Existing viewer assertions show a limited feature-by-feature distinction for unknown dictionary entries and unsupported objects. The broader Annex I first-error recommendation and all object classes remain outside this bounded pass.
